c.tagline: Mountains, beaches, and rhythm in the air.

avoid.reason: Includes Cidade de Deus, Complexo do Alemão and much of the north and west zones. Rated "Do Not Travel" — avoid even on guided tours.
Lively by day and evening, but streets empty out late — muggings and phone theft rise once the bars close.
Copacabana and Ipanema sands are best left after sunset — opportunistic robbery is common once the crowds thin.

hood_desc: The iconic beachfront neighborhood with its sweeping crescent of sand, mosaic promenade and round-the-clock energy. Suits travelers who want the classic Rio beach scene, lively nightlife and easy access, though it is busy and touristy.

A stylish, upscale beach district made famous in song, with fashionable shops, restaurants and a beautiful beach framed by the Dois Irmaos peaks. Ideal for visitors wanting chic surroundings and vibrant seaside culture.

The most affluent and exclusive neighborhood, quieter and more refined than its neighbors, with fine dining, boutiques and a lovely beach. Best for travelers seeking upscale comfort and a calmer, polished vibe.
A bohemian hilltop district of cobbled streets, colonial mansions, artists' studios and sweeping city views. Perfect for a creative crowd wanting charm, history and an offbeat, arty atmosphere.

The historic center and Rio's raucous nightlife hub around the Lapa Arches, famed for samba clubs, live music and street parties. Great for night owls chasing music and dancing, best explored with care.
lodging: Santa Teresa Hotel Rio de Janeiro - MGallery Collection

water.note: Technically treated but old pipes mean bottled or filtered water is recommended for visitors.

transit.pay: Buy a rechargeable Jaé card (replacing the old RioCard) at metro stations to tap in on Metro, VLT, and BRT; some gates also accept contactless bank cards directly. A single Metro ride costs about R$7.90 (~$1.40).
transit.hours: Metro runs about 5am-midnight (until 1am Fri/Sat); there is no all-night rail service, so late-night travelers rely on buses or ride-hailing.

landmarks: Christ the Redeemer
The massive Art Deco statue atop Corcovado Mountain overlooking the city is Rio's most globally recognized symbol and a UNESCO-listed New7Wonder.
Sugarloaf Mountain
A granite peak reached by cable car offering panoramic sunset views over Guanabara Bay and the city skyline.
Copacabana Beach
The world-famous crescent beach lined with the iconic wave-patterned Avenida Atlântica promenade.
Ipanema Beach
A chic beachfront made famous by 'The Girl from Ipanema,' with striking sunset views toward Dois Irmãos peaks.
Selarón Steps
A vibrant mosaic staircase covered in thousands of colorful tiles from around the world, created by artist Jorge Selarón.
Tijuca National Park
The world's largest urban rainforest, home to waterfalls, hiking trails, and views toward Corcovado.
Maracanã Stadium
One of the world's most legendary football stadiums, host to two FIFA World Cup finals.
Theatro Municipal
A grand Belle Époque opera house modeled on the Paris Opéra, showcasing Rio's ornate architectural heritage.
Metropolitan Cathedral of Rio de Janeiro
A striking modernist cone-shaped cathedral with towering stained-glass windows.
Arcos da Lapa
A historic white aqueduct-turned-viaduct in the lively Lapa nightlife district, dramatically lit at night.

train.note: Brazil has no intercity passenger rail network — the only trains from Rio are SuperVia urban commuter lines from Central do Brasil station. For long-distance travel use buses or flights.

bus.note: International coaches leave from the Novo Rio bus terminal (Rodoviária do Rio) in Santo Cristo. The Buenos Aires run takes roughly 42-48 hours with border formalities at Uruguaiana/Paso de los Libres — carry your passport. Big domestic operators like Viação 1001, Util and Cometa also depart from Novo Rio.

ferry.note: No international ferries serve Rio — only cruise ships at Pier Mauá. CCR Barcas runs the local commuter ferry across Guanabara Bay to Niterói from Praça XV.

half.name: Petropolis
half.blurb: A cool mountain town of imperial palaces, grand cathedrals and leafy gardens once favored by Brazilian royalty.

half.name: Serra dos Orgaos National Park
half.blurb: A dramatic mountain park of jagged peaks, waterfalls and forest trails, including the famous God's Finger.

full.name: Buzios
full.blurb: A chic coastal resort peninsula strung with dozens of pretty beaches, boutiques and lively seaside restaurants.

full.name: Ilha Grande
full.blurb: A car-free tropical island of jungle trails, waterfalls and idyllic beaches lapped by turquoise water.

full.name: Arraial do Cabo
full.blurb: Often called Brazil's Caribbean for its dazzling white sands and vivid clear-blue coastal waters.

full.name: Angra dos Reis
full.blurb: A gateway to a stunning bay scattered with hundreds of green islands and secluded swimming coves.
